title: 06. Distributed Systems & Consistency: CAP Theorem & Distributed Consistency

sections.title: Detailed Explanation
sections.body:
### What is the CAP Theorem?

The **CAP Theorem** (Brewer's Theorem) states that a distributed data store can provide only **two out of three** guarantees simultaneously:

- **C** — **Consistency**: Every read receives the most recent write or an error
- **A** — **Availability**: Every request receives a non-error response (no guarantee it's the latest)
- **P** — **Partition Tolerance**: System continues to operate despite network partitions between nodes

### The Key Insight

Since **network partitions are inevitable** in distributed systems, you must choose between:

- **CP** (Consistency + Partition Tolerance): System may become unavailable during a partition but never returns stale data
- **AP** (Availability + Partition Tolerance): System stays available during a partition but may return stale data
- CA systems don't truly exist in distributed environments (partitions always happen)

### Beyond CAP: PACELC

**PACELC** extends CAP: If there's a **P**artition, choose **A**vailability or **C**onsistency; **E**lse (normal operation), choose **L**atency or **C**onsistency.

| System      | Partition (P) | Else (E) | Classification |
| ----------- | ------------- | -------- | -------------- |
| DynamoDB    | AP            | EL       | PA/EL          |
| Cassandra   | AP            | EL       | PA/EL          |
| MongoDB     | CP            | EC       | PC/EC          |
| PostgreSQL  | CP            | EC       | PC/EC          |
| CockroachDB | CP            | EC       | PC/EC          |

diagrams.title: CAP: what happens during a network partition
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  p["Network partition: node A cannot reach node B"] --> ch{"A write arrives at A. What now?"}
  ch -->|"choose Consistency (CP)"| cp["Reject or block the write until B is reachable"]
  ch -->|"choose Availability (AP)"| ap["Accept the write; reconcile with B later"]
  cp --> cpx["Banking, inventory, leader election — ZooKeeper, etcd, Spanner"]
  ap --> apx["Feeds, carts, likes — Cassandra, DynamoDB"]
  ap --> rec["Conflict resolution: last-write-wins, vector clocks, CRDTs"]
diagrams.explain: Partitions are not optional in a distributed system, so the real choice is what to do *while* one is happening. A **CP** system refuses requests it cannot make consistent — correct but sometimes unavailable. An **AP** system keeps answering and repairs divergence afterwards — always up but sometimes stale. PACELC adds the everyday case: even without a partition you trade latency for consistency.

### The CAP Triangle

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                            CAP THEOREM                                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

                          CONSISTENCY
                              ▲
                             /|\
                            / | \
                           /  |  \
                          /   |   \
                         / CP |    \
                        / Zone|     \
                       /      |      \
                      / Bank  | Mongo \
                     / HBase  |       \
                    /─────────┼────────\
                   /   CA     |   AP    \
                  /  (myth in |  Zone   \
                 / distributed|         \
                / systems)    |Cassandra \
               /   Single    | DynamoDB  \
              /   Server DB  |  Riak     \
             ▼───────────────┴────────────▼
         AVAILABILITY ◄──────────────► PARTITION
                                        TOLERANCE

    ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  YOU MUST PICK 2 (and P is non-negotiable):            │
    │                                                         │
    │  CP: Consistent & Partition-Tolerant                    │
    │      → May REFUSE requests during partition             │
    │      → Banks, inventory, primary databases              │
    │                                                         │
    │  AP: Available & Partition-Tolerant                      │
    │      → May return STALE data during partition            │
    │      → Social media, DNS, caching                       │
    │                                                         │
    │  CA: Consistent & Available (NO partition tolerance)     │
    │      → Only works on single node (not distributed)      │
    │      → Traditional RDBMS on single server                │
    └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### What Happens During a Network Partition

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    NETWORK PARTITION SCENARIO                                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  NORMAL OPERATION:
  ┌──────────┐     ┌──────────┐     ┌──────────┐
  │  Node A  │◄───▶│  Node B  │◄───▶│  Node C  │
  │  Data: 5 │     │  Data: 5 │     │  Data: 5 │
  └──────────┘     └──────────┘     └──────────┘
                All nodes in sync ✓

  PARTITION OCCURS: (Network split between B and C)
  ┌──────────┐     ┌──────────┐  ╳  ┌──────────┐
  │  Node A  │◄───▶│  Node B  │  ╳  │  Node C  │
  │  Data: 5 │     │  Data: 5 │  ╳  │  Data: 5 │
  └──────────┘     └──────────┘  ╳  └──────────┘
                                 ╳
       Partition 1               ╳   Partition 2

  Client writes Data = 10 to Node A:

  ╔════════════════════════════════╗  ╔══════════════════════════════╗
  ║  CP CHOICE (Consistency)       ║  ║  AP CHOICE (Availability)    ║
  ║                                ║  ║                              ║
  ║  Node A: Data = 10 ✓          ║  ║  Node A: Data = 10 ✓        ║
  ║  Node B: Data = 10 ✓          ║  ║  Node B: Data = 10 ✓        ║
  ║  Node C: REFUSES requests ✗   ║  ║  Node C: Data = 5 (stale!) ✓║
  ║                                ║  ║                              ║
  ║  → Node C unavailable          ║  ║  → Node C returns old data   ║
  ║  → No inconsistency            ║  ║  → All nodes available       ║
  ║  → Some requests fail          ║  ║  → Temporary inconsistency   ║
  ╚════════════════════════════════╝  ╚══════════════════════════════╝
```

### Consistency Models Spectrum

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     CONSISTENCY SPECTRUM                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  STRONG                                                          WEAK
  CONSISTENCY                                                     CONSISTENCY
    │                                                                │
    ▼                                                                ▼
    ┌────────┬──────────┬───────────┬───────────┬──────────┬────────┐
    │Lineari-│Sequential│ Causal    │ Read-your │ Monotonic│Eventual│
    │zable   │Consistent│Consistency│  -writes  │  reads   │Consist.│
    └────────┴──────────┴───────────┴───────────┴──────────┴────────┘

    ◄─── Slower, more coordination ──── Faster, less coordination ──►
    ◄─── More correct ──────────────── More available ─────────────►

    LINEARIZABLE:
    • Every operation appears to happen atomically at one point in time
    • Most expensive, requires coordination
    • Example: CockroachDB, Spanner

    EVENTUAL CONSISTENCY:
    • If no new writes, all replicas converge to same value
    • Cheapest, most available
    • Example: DNS, Cassandra (default)

    CAUSAL CONSISTENCY:
    • Operations that are causally related are seen in order
    • Good balance of correctness and performance
    • Example: MongoDB (with causal sessions)
```

### PACELC Theorem

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         PACELC THEOREM                                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

                    ┌─────────────────────────┐
                    │   Is there a Network    │
                    │     PARTITION?          │
                    └─────────┬───────────────┘
                              │
                   ┌──────────┴──────────┐
                   │ YES                 │ NO
                   ▼                     ▼
          ┌────────────────┐    ┌────────────────┐
          │  Choose:       │    │  Choose:       │
          │  A or C?       │    │  L or C?       │
          ├────────────────┤    ├────────────────┤
          │ A: Available   │    │ L: Low Latency │
          │ C: Consistent  │    │ C: Consistent  │
          └────────────────┘    └────────────────┘

    Database Examples:
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ DynamoDB:  PA/EL (Availability + Low Latency)       │
    │ Cassandra: PA/EL (Availability + Low Latency)       │
    │ MongoDB:   PC/EC (Consistency + Consistency)         │
    │ Spanner:   PC/EC (Consistency + Consistency)         │
    │ PNUTS:     PC/EL (Consistency + Low Latency)         │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: 5 Real-World Examples
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- CP System: Banking service that prioritizes CONSISTENCY Cannot afford showing wrong balance, will sacrifice availability
- Chooses Consistency over Availability - Uses distributed locks to ensure only one write at a time - Will REJECT requests if can't guarantee…
- Transfer money with strong consistency guarantee If any step fails, everything rolls back
- Read from PRIMARY to guarantee latest balance If primary is down → return ERROR (not stale data)
- Acquire distributed lock — blocks other transfers
- Read latest balances from PRIMARY only (not replicas)
- Write with version check (optimistic concurrency)
- Wait for replicas to confirm (synchronous replication)

**Defines:** `Account`, `CPBankingService`, `APSocialTimeline`, `ConsistencyLevel`, `AdaptiveConsistencyStore`, `PartitionState`, `PartitionDetector`, `PartitionAwareService`, `ConsistencyReport`, `DistributedConsistencyChecker`

### Example 1: CP System — Bank Account Service

```python
"""
CP System: Banking service that prioritizes CONSISTENCY
Cannot afford showing wrong balance, will sacrifice availability
"""
import threading
import time
from typing import Optional
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Account:
    id: str
    balance: float
    version: int

class CPBankingService:
    """
    Chooses Consistency over Availability
    - Uses distributed locks to ensure only one write at a time
    - Will REJECT requests if can't guarantee consistency
    - Appropriate for: banking, inventory, payments
    """

    def __init__(self, distributed_lock, primary_db, replicas: list):
        self.lock = distributed_lock
        self.primary = primary_db
        self.replicas = replicas

    def transfer(self, from_account: str, to_account: str, amount: float) -> dict:
        """
        Transfer money with strong consistency guarantee
        If any step fails, everything rolls back
        """
        lock_key = f"transfer:{sorted([from_account, to_account])}"

        # Acquire distributed lock — blocks other transfers
        if not self.lock.acquire(lock_key, timeout=5):
            return {"status": "error", "message": "System busy, try again"}

        try:
            # Read latest balances from PRIMARY only (not replicas)
            sender = self._read_from_primary(from_account)
            receiver = self._read_from_primary(to_account)

            if not sender or not receiver:
                return {"status": "error", "message": "Account not found"}

            if sender.balance < amount:
                return {"status": "error", "message": "Insufficient funds"}

            # Write with version check (optimistic concurrency)
            success = self._atomic_transfer(sender, receiver, amount)

            if success:
                # Wait for replicas to confirm (synchronous replication)
                self._wait_for_replica_sync(timeout=3)
                return {"status": "success", "new_balance": sender.balance - amount}
            else:
                return {"status": "error", "message": "Concurrent modification"}
        finally:
            self.lock.release(lock_key)

    def get_balance(self, account_id: str) -> Optional[float]:
        """
        Read from PRIMARY to guarantee latest balance
        If primary is down → return ERROR (not stale data)
        """
        try:
            account = self._read_from_primary(account_id)
            return account.balance if account else None
        except ConnectionError:
            # CP choice: return error instead of stale replica data
            raise Exception("Service temporarily unavailable")

    def _read_from_primary(self, account_id: str) -> Optional[Account]:
        return self.primary.get(f"account:{account_id}")

    def _atomic_transfer(self, sender: Account, receiver: Account, amount: float) -> bool:
        """Atomic transfer using transaction + version check"""
        # BEGIN TRANSACTION
        # UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - amount, version = version + 1
        #   WHERE id = sender.id AND version = sender.version
        # UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + amount, version = version + 1
        #   WHERE id = receiver.id AND version = receiver.version
        # COMMIT
        return True  # Simplified

    def _wait_for_replica_sync(self, timeout: int):
        """Wait for all replicas to confirm write (synchronous replication)"""
        deadline = time.time() + timeout
        while time.time() < deadline:
            if self._all_replicas_synced():
                return
            time.sleep(0.1)
        raise Exception("Replica sync timeout — data may be inconsistent")

    def _all_replicas_synced(self) -> bool:
        return True  # Simplified
```

### Example 2: AP System — Social Media Timeline

```python
"""
AP System: Social media timeline that prioritizes AVAILABILITY
Better to show slightly stale feed than show nothing
"""
from datetime import datetime
from typing import List
import random
import json

class APSocialTimeline:
    """
    Chooses Availability over Consistency
    - Always returns data (even if slightly stale)
    - Uses eventual consistency
    - Appropriate for: social feeds, like counts, view counts
    """

    def __init__(self, local_cache, replicated_db, message_queue):
        self.cache = local_cache
        self.db = replicated_db
        self.queue = message_queue

    def post_tweet(self, user_id: str, content: str) -> dict:
        """
        Create a tweet — eventual consistency for followers' timelines
        """
        tweet = {
            "id": f"tweet_{int(datetime.utcnow().timestamp() * 1000)}",
            "user_id": user_id,
            "content": content,
            "timestamp": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
            "likes": 0
        }

        # Write to closest/local database node (async replication)
        self.db.write(f"tweet:{tweet['id']}", tweet)

        # Cache locally for read-your-writes
        self.cache.set(f"user_recent:{user_id}", tweet, ttl=60)

        # Fan-out to followers' timelines asynchronously
        self.queue.publish("timeline_updates", {
            "action": "new_tweet",
            "tweet": tweet,
            "user_id": user_id
        })

        return {"status": "success", "tweet_id": tweet["id"]}

    def get_timeline(self, user_id: str) -> List[dict]:
        """
        Get user's timeline — always returns SOMETHING
        Even during partitions, returns cached/local data
        """
        # Try 1: Local cache (fastest)
        cached = self.cache.get(f"timeline:{user_id}")
        if cached:
            return cached

        # Try 2: Any available database node (may be stale)
        try:
            timeline = self.db.read_from_any_node(f"timeline:{user_id}")
            if timeline:
                self.cache.set(f"timeline:{user_id}", timeline, ttl=30)
                return timeline
        except Exception:
            pass

        # Try 3: Return last known timeline (stale but available)
        stale_timeline = self.cache.get_stale(f"timeline:{user_id}")
        if stale_timeline:
            return stale_timeline

        # Absolute fallback: empty timeline (still available!)
        return []

    def like_tweet(self, tweet_id: str, user_id: str) -> dict:
        """
        Like count is eventually consistent
        Multiple users may like simultaneously — counters may temporarily
        disagree across nodes — that's OK!
        """
        # Increment locally (eventual consistency)
        self.db.increment(f"likes:{tweet_id}", 1)

        # Different nodes may show different counts temporarily
        # Eventually they'll all converge to the same value

        return {"status": "liked"}

    def get_like_count(self, tweet_id: str) -> int:
        """
        May return slightly stale count — that's acceptable
        """
        try:
            count = self.db.read_from_any_node(f"likes:{tweet_id}")
            return count or 0
        except Exception:
            cached_count = self.cache.get(f"likes:{tweet_id}")
            return cached_count or 0
```

### Example 3: Consistency Level Selector

```python
"""
System that dynamically selects consistency level based on operation type
"""
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any, Optional

class ConsistencyLevel(Enum):
    ONE = "one"          # Read/write from 1 node
    QUORUM = "quorum"    # Majority of nodes
    ALL = "all"          # All nodes
    LOCAL_QUORUM = "local_quorum"  # Majority in local DC

class AdaptiveConsistencyStore:
    """
    Different operations need different consistency levels
    """

    def __init__(self, cluster_nodes: list, replication_factor: int = 3):
        self.nodes = cluster_nodes
        self.rf = replication_factor

    def write(self, key: str, value: Any, consistency: ConsistencyLevel) -> bool:
        """Write with specified consistency"""
        required_acks = self._get_required_nodes(consistency)
        acks = 0

        for node in self._get_replica_nodes(key):
            try:
                node.write(key, value)
                acks += 1
                if acks >= required_acks:
                    return True
            except Exception:
                continue

        return acks >= required_acks

    def read(self, key: str, consistency: ConsistencyLevel) -> Optional[Any]:
        """Read with specified consistency"""
        required_reads = self._get_required_nodes(consistency)
        results = []

        for node in self._get_replica_nodes(key):
            try:
                value = node.read(key)
                results.append(value)
                if len(results) >= required_reads:
                    break
            except Exception:
                continue

        if len(results) < required_reads:
            raise Exception(f"Could not achieve {consistency.value} consistency")

        # Return most recent value (by version/timestamp)
        return self._get_latest(results)

    def _get_required_nodes(self, consistency: ConsistencyLevel) -> int:
        mapping = {
            ConsistencyLevel.ONE: 1,
            ConsistencyLevel.QUORUM: (self.rf // 2) + 1,
            ConsistencyLevel.ALL: self.rf,
            ConsistencyLevel.LOCAL_QUORUM: (self.rf // 2) + 1,
        }
        return mapping[consistency]

    def _get_replica_nodes(self, key: str):
        """Get nodes responsible for this key"""
        hash_val = hash(key) % len(self.nodes)
        return [self.nodes[(hash_val + i) % len(self.nodes)] for i in range(self.rf)]

    def _get_latest(self, results: list) -> Any:
        return max(results, key=lambda r: r.get("version", 0) if isinstance(r, dict) else 0)

# Usage patterns by operation type:
store = AdaptiveConsistencyStore(cluster_nodes=[], replication_factor=3)

# Payment processing — MUST be consistent
store.write("balance:user1", {"amount": 100, "version": 1}, ConsistencyLevel.QUORUM)
store.read("balance:user1", ConsistencyLevel.QUORUM)

# Social media likes — eventual consistency OK
store.write("likes:post1", {"count": 42, "version": 1}, ConsistencyLevel.ONE)
store.read("likes:post1", ConsistencyLevel.ONE)

# User profile update — read-your-writes needed
store.write("profile:user1", {"name": "Alice", "version": 1}, ConsistencyLevel.QUORUM)
store.read("profile:user1", ConsistencyLevel.QUORUM)
```

### Example 4: Partition Detector and Handler

```python
"""
Detect and handle network partitions gracefully
"""
import threading
import time
from enum import Enum
from typing import List, Dict, Callable

class PartitionState(Enum):
    NORMAL = "normal"
    SUSPECTED = "suspected"
    CONFIRMED = "confirmed"

class PartitionDetector:
    """Detects network partitions using heartbeats"""

    def __init__(self, nodes: List[str], heartbeat_interval: float = 2.0,
                 failure_threshold: int = 3):
        self.nodes = nodes
        self.interval = heartbeat_interval
        self.threshold = failure_threshold
        self.missed_heartbeats: Dict[str, int] = {n: 0 for n in nodes}
        self.state = PartitionState.NORMAL
        self.handlers: Dict[PartitionState, List[Callable]] = {
            s: [] for s in PartitionState
        }

    def on_state_change(self, state: PartitionState, handler: Callable):
        self.handlers[state].append(handler)

    def check_heartbeats(self):
        """Check all nodes and update partition state"""
        for node in self.nodes:
            if self._ping(node):
                self.missed_heartbeats[node] = 0
            else:
                self.missed_heartbeats[node] += 1

        # Determine partition state
        unreachable = sum(
            1 for n in self.nodes if self.missed_heartbeats[n] >= self.threshold
        )
        total = len(self.nodes)

        if unreachable == 0:
            new_state = PartitionState.NORMAL
        elif unreachable < total // 2:
            new_state = PartitionState.SUSPECTED
        else:
            new_state = PartitionState.CONFIRMED

        if new_state != self.state:
            old_state = self.state
            self.state = new_state
            self._trigger_handlers(new_state)

    def _ping(self, node: str) -> bool:
        """Try to reach a node"""
        try:
            # Actual implementation: TCP connect or HTTP health check
            return True
        except Exception:
            return False

    def _trigger_handlers(self, state: PartitionState):
        for handler in self.handlers[state]:
            handler()

class PartitionAwareService:
    """Service that adapts behavior based on partition state"""

    def __init__(self, detector: PartitionDetector):
        self.detector = detector
        self.mode = "normal"  # normal, degraded, read_only

        detector.on_state_change(PartitionState.NORMAL, self._resume_normal)
        detector.on_state_change(PartitionState.SUSPECTED, self._enter_degraded)
        detector.on_state_change(PartitionState.CONFIRMED, self._enter_readonly)

    def handle_request(self, request: dict) -> dict:
        if self.mode == "read_only" and request.get("method") in ("POST", "PUT", "DELETE"):
            return {"error": "Service in read-only mode due to network partition", "code": 503}

        if self.mode == "degraded":
            # Use local cache, warn about potential staleness
            return self._handle_degraded(request)

        return self._handle_normal(request)

    def _resume_normal(self):
        self.mode = "normal"
        print("Partition resolved — resuming normal operations")

    def _enter_degraded(self):
        self.mode = "degraded"
        print("Potential partition — entering degraded mode")

    def _enter_readonly(self):
        self.mode = "read_only"
        print("Partition confirmed — entering read-only mode")

    def _handle_normal(self, request: dict) -> dict:
        return {"status": "ok", "mode": "normal"}

    def _handle_degraded(self, request: dict) -> dict:
        return {"status": "ok", "mode": "degraded", "warning": "data may be stale"}
```

### Example 5: Consistency Checker Tool

```python
"""
Tool to verify consistency across distributed nodes
"""
import time
import hashlib
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class ConsistencyReport:
    total_keys_checked: int
    consistent_keys: int
    inconsistent_keys: int
    consistency_percentage: float
    inconsistencies: List[dict]
    check_duration_seconds: float

class DistributedConsistencyChecker:
    """
    Checks whether data is consistent across all nodes
    Useful for monitoring AP systems
    """

    def __init__(self, nodes: list):
        self.nodes = nodes

    def full_consistency_check(self, sample_keys: List[str] = None) -> ConsistencyReport:
        """Run consistency check across all nodes"""
        start_time = time.time()
        inconsistencies = []

        if sample_keys is None:
            sample_keys = self._get_sample_keys(1000)

        consistent = 0
        inconsistent = 0

        for key in sample_keys:
            values = {}
            for node in self.nodes:
                try:
                    val = node.read(key)
                    values[node.id] = val
                except Exception:
                    values[node.id] = None

            # Check if all values match
            unique_values = set(str(v) for v in values.values() if v is not None)

            if len(unique_values) <= 1:
                consistent += 1
            else:
                inconsistent += 1
                inconsistencies.append({
                    "key": key,
                    "values_by_node": values,
                    "unique_values": len(unique_values)
                })

        total = consistent + inconsistent
        return ConsistencyReport(
            total_keys_checked=total,
            consistent_keys=consistent,
            inconsistent_keys=inconsistent,
            consistency_percentage=(consistent / total * 100) if total > 0 else 100,
            inconsistencies=inconsistencies[:50],  # Limit report size
            check_duration_seconds=time.time() - start_time
        )

    def check_write_propagation(self, timeout_seconds: float = 10) -> dict:
        """
        Write to one node, check how long until all nodes see it
        """
        test_key = f"_consistency_check_{int(time.time())}"
        test_value = f"test_{time.time()}"

        # Write to first node
        self.nodes[0].write(test_key, test_value)
        write_time = time.time()

        # Check other nodes
        propagation_times = {}
        remaining_nodes = set(range(1, len(self.nodes)))

        while remaining_nodes and (time.time() - write_time) < timeout_seconds:
            for i in list(remaining_nodes):
                try:
                    val = self.nodes[i].read(test_key)
                    if val == test_value:
                        propagation_times[self.nodes[i].id] = time.time() - write_time
                        remaining_nodes.remove(i)
                except Exception:
                    pass
            time.sleep(0.1)

        return {
            "propagation_times": propagation_times,
            "timed_out_nodes": [self.nodes[i].id for i in remaining_nodes],
            "all_consistent": len(remaining_nodes) == 0,
            "max_lag_seconds": max(propagation_times.values()) if propagation_times else None
        }

    def _get_sample_keys(self, count: int) -> List[str]:
        """Get random sample of keys from first node"""
        return self.nodes[0].get_random_keys(count)
```

quiz.question: What is eventual consistency? Give a real-world example.
options: Linearizability is the strongest consistency model — every operation appears to happen atomically at a single point in time, and all clients see operations in the same order.

Eventual consistency means if no new updates are made, all replicas will eventually converge to the same value.
quiz.explanation: Eventual consistency means if no new updates are made, all replicas will eventually converge to the same value. Real example: DNS — when you update a DNS record, it takes time (minutes to hours) to propagate globally. During propagation, different users may see different IPs, but eventually all see the updated record.

quiz.question: How does Netflix handle the CAP trade-off?
options: Cassandra is tunable consistency. Default is AP (eventual), but you can configure per-query: ONE (fastest, least consistent), QUORUM (majority must agree), ALL (strongest, slowest).

quiz.explanation: Netflix primarily uses AP (availability over consistency). If there's a partition: (1) User can still browse and play cached content, (2) Watch history may be slightly stale, (3) Recommendations use cached data. They use Cassandra (AP) for most data, with eventual consistency acceptable for viewing history and preferences.
